purpose: Replace mistaken dolphin identity with existing gray shark; rebuild original mouth anatomy.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw Image 1, the exact original SLEVEJM2 003 sprite, as one polished cartoon SHARK sprite. Image 1 controls pose, mouth shape, facing, visible anatomy, framing and water occlusion. Images 2 and 3 are CHARACTER DESIGN AND DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not pose. Match the established shark: neutral medium gray skin, pale ivory jaw and underside, gill slits, bold black outlines, smooth restrained cel shading, heavy sly brows and razor-sharp triangular teeth. This is the sneaky shark character, never a friendly dolphin; no dolphin beak or rounded dolphin teeth. Pose: Upright shark in right-facing rear three-quarter view, high rounded back and compact upper snout. Its mouth is open, lined with sharp triangular teeth; the exaggerated lower jaw projects forward and upward to the right, slightly lower than in an extreme upturned pose. Small sly eye stays on upper head, above the tooth-filled opening. Mostly gray back/flank with narrow pale belly at right. Dorsal fin extends back-left, near pectoral fin hangs against the gray flank. Exact source body height and original waterline. Preserve the source silhouette and relative positions while replacing pixel steps with smooth ink. Only the character parts above water are drawn, with a thin cyan-and-white ripple at original cutoff. Do not complete submerged body, tail or legs. One character only. All contours inside canvas with clear transparent padding on every edge. Actual transparent RGBA background, no checkerboard, scene, cast shadow, glow, text or collage.
